verdict: Below threshold (5.5 < 7.5): do not pass the quality gate. The revised paper is unusually transparent and internally consistent; the numbers I spot-checked (abstract ranges, Holm counts, best-heuristic margins, H5b slope conversions, B-spread vs Random, agreement trends, latency range) match Tables 1-5. But the paper is still a preliminary, planar-simulation, negative-result measurement with a narrow contribution. Its headline test split is too underpowered to decide the primary question, and the most relevant baseline, a reduced planner, is unevaluated in 4/5 cells. Three citation placeholders remain unresolved, and Figure 1 exists only as a generation prompt with an empty data panel. The remaining problems are partly about the writing and partly about missing evidence. Fixing only the writing would not lift the score to the threshold.
strengths: Pre-registration is strict and documented. Every decision row traces to a frozen rule (amendment v5.0 and addenda v5.1c-f). Report-only, exploratory and post-hoc values are labelled throughout, and the deviations (test5 cut from 500 to 300, missing frontier figure, flip rates only for seed 701, rl_success truncation) are stated openly in Section 4.

The negative result is reported honestly and with calibrated language: 'not supported', 'not detected, not absent', and '~7 pp not excluded' for H5b. The paper does not oversell equivalence from small test5 point gaps and explains why test5 cannot decide a match.

The internal numerical consistency is high. The abstract, Findings, Table 1, Table 2a/2b, Table 3, Table 4/4b and Table 5 agree on the 3.2-6.0 pp and 0.2-2.5 pp gaps, 4/5 Holm wins over H*, the +3.5 to +14.5 pp post-hoc margins, the 2,523-9,933x latency range, and the slope and its span conversion (-0.104 x 0.71 rad = about -7.4 pp).

The design is careful. It uses paired episodes across methods, a crossed episode x seed bootstrap, Holm applied only to the two registered families, and the same DeepSets head and action set for distillation and RL, which isolates the training signal as intended.

Useful methods observations are separated from decision rows: the evaluator-resolution check (E5, 6.5-8% flips, comparable to the test5 gap), the ordering disagreement between the contrastive bound and the posterior read-out, the look-ahead headroom with its max-selection bias (E7), and the point that DAgger checkpoint selection on G*-visited decisions cannot register DAgger's benefit.

The limitations section is comprehensive. It covers G* run once, validation rows drawn from three rounds, the three-way A16 confound, re-used labels, the overlap between A16 and the earlier library A, and the one-directional inversion check.
weaknesses: [paper-level] Three unresolved citation placeholders remain: DeepSets (Zaheer et al. 2017) in 3.3, Holm (1979) in 4, and bootstrap/Efron in 4. The manuscript is not submission-ready as is.

[paper-level] Figure 1 exists only as an image-generation prompt and a matplotlib spec. Panel D is an empty placeholder, and the caption depends on a figure that has not been produced. The paper's only figure is not actually in the paper.

[paper-level] The prose reads like an internal lab record rather than a paper. It is dense with project-internal identifiers (addendum v5.1f, E5/E6/E7, cfg 6, val3/test5/pilot3/cal3, gt3, rule reading 0.975), source-file paths, and multi-clause sentences; the abstract runs to about 230 words of qualifiers. A reader outside the project cannot follow the narrative without the amendments.

[paper-level] The contribution is narrow and largely negative. As the paper admits, distilling an information-gathering expert and amortizing design by RL are both established. The main result is a failed gate in a planar simulator with 3-4 probes per episode, and the paper does not argue convincingly why the community should care about this specific measurement.

[paper-level] The gate D5 is calibrated so that it can hardly pass. At the observed SEs, the effective clause-(i) threshold is -1.2 to -1.7 pp against a nominal delta of 4 pp, so a cell with a -3.6 pp deficit fails. The paper notes this, but it does not discuss whether 'gate fails in 5/5' says more about the gate than about amortization, which weakens the headline C1.

[evidence-level] The primary test split is underpowered. With 300 episodes per method and cell, the student-G* CIs are 9.6-12.3 pp wide against a 4 pp margin, so H5a can decide neither a match nor a shortfall. No equivalence test was run, and no pooled estimate was computed.
[evidence-level] G* was run once per cell, so the teacher's run-to-run Monte Carlo variance is missing from every student-G* interval. Those intervals may be too narrow, and this was not measured.

[evidence-level] The cheapest alternative to learning, a reduced planner (g125_512_16, g500_512_4), is timed in every cell but evaluated for accuracy only in S12, from a previous round on a different split with different students. The central practical question, whether learning is needed for a fast policy at all, is left unanswered in 4/5 cells.

[evidence-level] The RL comparator is weak. One configuration was chosen by a single-seed sweep on S2 and reused everywhere; it collapses in A16-2, which is the only cell where H2-v5 holds. Whether it is under-tuned in S4/S8/S12 was not tested, so C3 says little about distillation versus RL.

[evidence-level] The heuristic baselines are weak or poorly selected. H* is not the best test5 heuristic in 4/5 cells, and the margins over the best heuristic are post hoc with no CI. B-spread scores below Random in 4/5 cells, and no cheap information-based heuristic is included.

[evidence-level] The DAgger component is not shown to matter. Kept held-out regret in rounds r0 and r2 overlaps in every cell, and regret on student-visited states, which is the quantity DAgger targets, was not measured. The deployed student cannot be told apart from behaviour cloning.

[evidence-level] The evaluator-resolution check (E5) covers 2 cells, 200 episodes and one student seed. It shifts the seed-701 contrast by about 0.8x to 2x the test5 gap, and its effect on the 5-seed test5 contrasts is unknown. This undermines every success contrast.

[evidence-level] The A16-2 cell confounds shape family, K and n* (and shares 8 identities with the earlier library A), and it is run at a single kappa. H5b is a 5-point regression with weights estimated from test5. The regime question (C4) is therefore effectively unanswerable from this design.

[paper-level] The latency speed-up (2,523-9,933x) is per decision of compute, with the CI rule met in only 1/5 cells, timings from one student seed, and runners that differ across cells. No task-time model is given, so its practical significance is unclear. It should not appear in the abstract and conclusion without that qualifier made prominent.

[paper-level] Some presentation issues remain. Table 4b appears before Table 4. The inversion check tests only one direction, a gap between the registered and the implemented rule that is disclosed only in a methods aside. The validation G* rows mix three rounds, yet the validation gaps are compared across cells as if they came from one source.
required_actions: [paper-level] Resolve all three [CITE-MISSING] placeholders (Zaheer et al. 2017 DeepSets; Holm 1979; Efron/Efron-Tibshirani bootstrap) with verified bibliography entries.
[paper-level] Produce Figure 1 as an actual figure. Render panels A-C and plot panel D from results_v5.json as specified, and remove the generation prompt and plotting spec from the manuscript body.

[paper-level] Rewrite for an external reader. Replace internal identifiers (addendum labels, E-numbers, cfg indices, split codenames, file paths) with descriptive names or move them to an appendix or provenance table. Shorten the abstract to its core claims, and cut repeated qualifier chains in the Introduction, Findings and Conclusion.

[paper-level] Add an explicit discussion of the gate's calibration. Explain that the effective clause-(i) threshold of about -1.2 to -1.7 pp is much stricter than delta = 4 pp. State what fraction of plausible true deficits inside the margin would pass, and frame C1 accordingly.

[paper-level] Sharpen the motivation and the significance argument. State concretely what a practitioner or a BED researcher should do differently given these results, or reposition the work explicitly as a short negative-results or workshop contribution.

[evidence-level] Evaluate the reduced-G* configurations for accuracy on test5 in all five cells, paired with the v5 student, and draw the registered latency-accuracy frontier. Without this, the 'cheap policy' contribution (C2) cannot be weighed against its obvious alternative.
[evidence-level] Increase test5 power enough to make H5a decidable, or run a formal equivalence (TOST) test. At minimum, restore the registered 500 episodes per method and cell.

[evidence-level] Rerun G* at least once more per cell, with an independent Monte Carlo seed, so that teacher variance enters the student-G* intervals. Report G* self-agreement as the ceiling for the action-agreement read-out.
[evidence-level] Tune RL per cell, or at least in A16-2 and one high-kappa S cell, with more than one seed in the sweep, before drawing any distillation-versus-RL conclusion.

[evidence-level] Measure label regret on student-visited states, and compare the deployed student against its round-r0 (behaviour-cloning) checkpoint on success, to establish whether DAgger contributes anything.
[evidence-level] Extend the evaluator-resolution check to all cells and all five student seeds on test5, or adopt the finer evaluator, so that success contrasts are not dominated by read-out flips.
[evidence-level] Add a cheap information-based heuristic baseline, and report the student against the best heuristic with a proper CI, chosen on a larger pilot or with selection accounted for.

[evidence-level] To answer the regime question, add A16 cells at additional kappa values, or a library that varies one factor at a time, so that travel-cost effects can be separated from library effects.
